```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r load-model}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wang_2024_leritrelvir"))
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2024.1449583> (open access; the
  NONMEM control stream and supplementary Tables S1-S3 are in Supplementary
  Material 1)

Leritrelvir (RAY1216) is an oral SARS-CoV-2 3CL (main) protease inhibitor
metabolised mainly by CYP3A. Wang 2024 pooled the first-in-human phase I study
(NCT05829551), in which leritrelvir was given alone or boosted with 100 mg
ritonavir, and used the resulting population PK model to choose between
400 mg three times daily (TID) alone and twice-daily (BID) dosing with
ritonavir. The 400 mg TID monotherapy regimen was taken into phase II and III.

# Population

`r ui$population$n_subjects` healthy Chinese adults (Wang 2024 Table 1): median
age 35 years (19-48), median weight 60.6 kg (48.2-90.8), median BMI 22.9 kg/m^2,
50% female, median creatinine clearance 115 mL/min. 1571 plasma concentrations
were analysed (150 of 1721, 8.72%, were below the LLOQ and excluded). The study
(Figure 1) had single-ascending-dose arms of 400, 800 and 1600 mg alone; a
200 mg alone then 200 mg + ritonavir crossover; an 800 mg (alone) and a
500 mg + ritonavir fasted/fed crossover; 300, 500 and 700 mg + ritonavir BID;
and 400 mg TID alone. The multiple-dose arms dosed for 4 days plus a single
morning dose on day 5. Each crossover subject was coded as two NONMEM IDs
(102 IDs in total).

```{r population}
str(ui$population)
```

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source |

| Structure: 2-compartment, first-order elimination | ADVAN4 TRANS4 | Results 3.2.1; supplement control stream |
| Sequential zero-order (D1) then first-order (Ka) absorption, with lag | `dur(depot)`, `alag(depot)` | Results 3.2.1; Discussion; control stream `D1`, `ALAG1` |
| Separate typical values alone vs with ritonavir | `IF (RTV.EQ.0)` | Results 3.2.1; control stream |
| `lcl`, `lcl_boosted` | 44.4, 12.2 L/h | Table 2 CL Mono / Comb |
| `lvc`, `lvc_boosted` | 18.9, 9.78 L | Table 2 Vc Mono / Comb |
| `lka`, `lka_boosted` | 0.293, 0.169 1/h | Table 2 Ka Mono / Comb |
| `lq`, `lq_boosted` | 5.57, 0.611 L/h | Table 2 Q Mono / Comb |
| `lvp`, `lvp_boosted` | 58.2, 9.30 L | Table 2 Vp Mono / Comb |
| `ld1`, `ld1_boosted` | 0.0722, 0.0684 h | Table 2 D1 Mono / Comb |
| `ltlag`, `ltlag_boosted` | 0.189, 0.166 h | Table 2 ALAG1 Mono / Comb |
| `lfdepot` | log(1), fixed | Table 2 F1 = 1 FIX |
| `e_fed_fdepot` | 0.409 | Results 3.2.1 F1 equation; Table 2 F1.FED = 1.51 |
| `e_fed_ka` | 0.291 | Results 3.2.1 Ka equation; control stream THETA(17) |
| `e_fed_d1` | 3.14 | Results 3.2.1 D1 equation; control stream THETA(16) |
| `e_sexf_cl` | -0.224 | Results 3.2.1 CL equation; Table 2 CL.sex = 0.800 |
| `e_occ1_cl` | -0.469 | Results 3.2.1 CL equation; Table 2 CL.OC1.INH = 0.626 |
| `e_occ2_cl` | 0.412 | Results 3.2.1 CL equation; Table 2 CL.OC2.IND = 1.51 |
| Occasion indicators OC1 (t >= 12 h), OC2 (t >= 96 h), multiple-dose only | `oc1`, `oc2` | Control stream `IF (DOSESCH.GT.1.AND.TIME.GE.12)` |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc`, `etalka`, `etalvp`, `etald1` | 30.6, 80.8, 26.1, 44.7, 155% | Table 2 IIV; variance = (IIV%/100)^2 |
| `etaiov_cl_1`, `etaiov_cl_2` | 19.3% | Table 2 OC1.CL (OC2.CL blank: SAME) |

# Typical-value behaviour

Single 400 mg doses of leritrelvir alone, and 200 mg with ritonavir, for a
typical male and female subject in the fasted and fed state. Every dose record
carries `rate = -2`, which is what makes rxode2 use the modelled zero-order
duration `dur(depot)`; without it the dose would enter the depot as a bolus.

```{r typical}
ui_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(ui)
grid_sd <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 4, by = 0.05), seq(4.25, 72, by = 0.25))))

typ_ev <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  scen = 1:8,
  time = grid_sd
) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central") |>
  bind_rows(tibble(scen = 1:8, time = 0, evid = 1L, rate = -2, cmt = "depot")) |>
  left_join(
    tibble(
      scen = 1:8,
      CONMED_RTV = rep(c(0L, 1L), each = 4),
      dose = rep(c(400, 200), each = 4),
      SEXF = rep(c(0L, 1L, 0L, 1L), 2),
      FED = rep(c(0L, 0L, 1L, 1L), 2)
    ),
    by = "scen"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    id = scen,
    amt = ifelse(evid == 1L, dose, 0),
    MULTI_DOSE = 0L
  ) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_typ, typ_ev, returnType = "data.frame", addDosing = FALSE,
                       keep = c("CONMED_RTV", "SEXF", "FED", "dose")) |>
  mutate(
    Regimen = ifelse(CONMED_RTV == 1, "200 mg + ritonavir", "400 mg alone"),
    Subject = paste(ifelse(SEXF == 1, "female", "male"), ifelse(FED == 1, "fed", "fasted"))
  )

ggplot(typ, aes(time, Cc, colour = Subject)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~Regimen) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Leritrelvir (ng/mL)",
       title = "Typical single-dose profiles")
```

The zero-order duration is short in the fasted state (0.072 h) and becomes
1.67 h with food (`0.0722 * exp(3.14)`). The check below confirms rxode2 is
spreading the fed dose over that window: half-way through it, the depot must
hold well under the full bioavailable dose, whereas a bolus would leave about
80% of it there.

```{r rate-check}
d1_fed <- exp(log(0.0722) + 3.14)
t_mid <- 0.189 + d1_fed / 2
depot_mid <- typ |> filter(id == 3) |> slice(which.min(abs(time - t_mid))) |> pull(depot)
f_fed <- exp(0.409)
stopifnot(depot_mid < 0.6 * f_fed * 400)
c(d1_fed = d1_fed, depot_at_mid = depot_mid, bioavailable_dose = f_fed * 400)
```

The AUC of a typical single dose must equal `F * dose / CL` in closed form,
which pins the clearance, the bioavailability and the mg-to-ng/mL scaling.

```{r closed-form-auc}
typ_nca_conc <- typ |> filter(!is.na(Cc)) |> select(id, time, Cc, Regimen, Subject)
typ_nca_dose <- typ_ev |> filter(evid == 1L) |> select(id, time, amt)
typ_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(typ_nca_conc, Cc ~ time | Regimen + Subject + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(typ_nca_dose, amt ~ time | id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
))
auc_closed <- typ_ev |>
  filter(evid == 1L) |>
  mutate(
    cl = ifelse(CONMED_RTV == 1, 12.2, 44.4) * exp(-0.224 * SEXF),
    auc_closed = 1000 * exp(0.409 * FED) * amt / cl
  ) |>
  select(id, auc_closed)
auc_cmp <- as.data.frame(typ_nca$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  left_join(auc_closed, by = "id") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES / auc_closed - 1))
auc_cmp |>
  select(Regimen, Subject, `AUCinf (ng*h/mL)` = PPORRES, `F*Dose/CL` = auc_closed, `% diff` = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
# Same parameters on both sides: only extrapolation and trapezoid error remain.
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_cmp$pct_diff) < 2))
```

# Replicating Supplementary Table S1 and Figure 4

Wang 2024 simulated 1000 fasted subjects (500 male, 500 female) per regimen:
leritrelvir alone 300, 400, 500 and 600 mg TID (08:00, 14:00, 20:00) for five
days, and 200 or 300 mg with ritonavir BID (08:00, 20:00), the BID arms
taking a single morning dose on day 5 (the 9th dose, Figure 4D). Here each
arm has 200 subjects (100 male, 100 female). The occasion indicators switch at
12 h and 96 h after the first dose (`MULTI_DOSE = 1`).

The four occasion random effects (`etaiov_*`) are set to zero for this
replication. With them included, the simulated 10th-90th percentile bands are
much wider than the published ones at every time after 12 h (the 90th
percentile about 25% above the paper's, up to 60%), while with them excluded
the bands agree to within a few percent at every row of Table S1. The
published simulation therefore appears to carry only the between-subject
variability. The occasion terms stay in the model; they are set to zero only
here.

```{r tables1-sim}
n_per_arm <- 200
arms <- tibble(
  arm = 1:6,
  Regimen = c("300 mg TID", "400 mg TID", "500 mg TID", "600 mg TID",
              "300 mg BID + RTV", "200 mg BID + RTV"),
  dose = c(300, 400, 500, 600, 300, 200),
  CONMED_RTV = c(0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 1L, 1L),
  tid = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)
)
dose_times_tid <- as.vector(outer(c(0, 6, 12), 24 * 0:4, "+"))
dose_times_bid <- seq(0, 96, by = 12)
obs_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.25), seq(96, 120, by = 0.25))))

subjects <- tibble(arm = rep(arms$arm, each = n_per_arm)) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), SEXF = rep(rep(c(0L, 1L), each = n_per_arm / 2), nrow(arms))) |>
  left_join(arms, by = "arm")

dose_rows <- bind_rows(
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = subjects$id[subjects$tid], time = dose_times_tid),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = subjects$id[!subjects$tid], time = dose_times_bid)
) |>
  mutate(evid = 1L, rate = -2, cmt = "depot")
obs_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = subjects$id, time = obs_grid) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, rate = 0, cmt = "central")

ev_s1 <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  left_join(subjects, by = "id") |>
  mutate(amt = ifelse(evid == 1L, dose, 0), FED = 0L, MULTI_DOSE = 1L) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, rate, cmt, CONMED_RTV, SEXF, FED, MULTI_DOSE)

ui_noiov <- ui |>
  rxode2::ini(
    etaiov_cl_1 ~ 1e-10, etaiov_cl_2 ~ 1e-10,
    etaiov_vc_1 ~ 1e-10, etaiov_vc_2 ~ 1e-10
  )

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240911)
sim_s1 <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_noiov, ev_s1, returnType = "data.frame", addDosing = FALSE) |>
  left_join(select(subjects, id, Regimen), by = "id")
```

```{r tables1-compare}
table_s1 <- tribble(
  ~Regimen,           ~dose_no, ~time, ~paper_med, ~paper_p10, ~paper_p90,
  "300 mg TID",        "1st",    6,    455,  269,  746,
  "300 mg TID",        "2nd",   12,    633,  373, 1019,
  "300 mg TID",        "3rd",   24,    311,  140,  650,
  "300 mg TID",        "13th", 102,    600,  332, 1017,
  "300 mg TID",        "14th", 108,    677,  375, 1148,
  "300 mg TID",        "15th", 120,    215,   96,  444,
  "400 mg TID",        "1st",    6,    624,  362, 1065,
  "400 mg TID",        "2nd",   12,    860,  491, 1447,
  "400 mg TID",        "3rd",   24,    436,  184,  976,
  "400 mg TID",        "13th", 102,    809,  448, 1508,
  "400 mg TID",        "14th", 108,    910,  501, 1711,
  "400 mg TID",        "15th", 120,    287,  119,  686,
  "500 mg TID",        "1st",    6,    762,  456, 1276,
  "500 mg TID",        "2nd",   12,   1035,  626, 1728,
  "500 mg TID",        "3rd",   24,    517,  245, 1124,
  "500 mg TID",        "13th", 102,    990,  562, 1750,
  "500 mg TID",        "14th", 108,   1115,  633, 1985,
  "500 mg TID",        "15th", 120,    343,  159,  761,
  "600 mg TID",        "1st",    6,    920,  569, 1528,
  "600 mg TID",        "2nd",   12,   1260,  771, 2106,
  "600 mg TID",        "3rd",   24,    633,  297, 1379,
  "600 mg TID",        "13th", 102,   1206,  713, 2138,
  "600 mg TID",        "14th", 108,   1360,  790, 2449,
  "600 mg TID",        "15th", 120,    426,  192,  942,
  "300 mg BID + RTV",  "1st",   12,    817,  446, 1395,
  "300 mg BID + RTV",  "2nd",   24,   1585,  807, 2862,
  "300 mg BID + RTV",  "9th",  108,   1047,  530, 2000,
  "200 mg BID + RTV",  "1st",   12,    543,  312,  911,

)

s1_sim <- sim_s1 |>
  filter(time %in% table_s1$time) |>
  group_by(Regimen, time) |>
  summarise(
    sim_med = median(Cc),
    sim_p10 = quantile(Cc, 0.1),
    sim_p90 = quantile(Cc, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
s1_cmp <- table_s1 |>
  left_join(s1_sim, by = c("Regimen", "time")) |>
  mutate(
    pct_med = 100 * (sim_med / paper_med - 1),
    pct_p10 = 100 * (sim_p10 / paper_p10 - 1),
    pct_p90 = 100 * (sim_p90 / paper_p90 - 1)
  )
stopifnot(nrow(s1_cmp) == 30, !anyNA(s1_cmp$sim_med))

s1_cmp |>
  transmute(
    Regimen, Dose = dose_no, `Time (h)` = time,
    `Paper median (P10-P90)` = sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", paper_med, paper_p10, paper_p90),
    `Simulated median (P10-P90)` = sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", sim_med, sim_p10, sim_p90),
    `% diff median` = round(pct_med, 1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Trough concentrations (ng/mL): Wang 2024 Supplementary Table S1 vs simulation.")
```

```{r tables1-gate}
c(
  median_pct_med = median(s1_cmp$pct_med),
  q90_abs_pct_med = unname(quantile(abs(s1_cmp$pct_med), 0.9)),
  median_abs_pct_p10 = median(abs(s1_cmp$pct_p10)),
  median_abs_pct_p90 = median(abs(s1_cmp$pct_p90))
)
stopifnot(
  # Centre: a mis-transcribed clearance, volume or occasion step moves the
  # whole set of troughs by tens of percent.
  abs(median(s1_cmp$pct_med)) < 6,
  # Envelope over the 30 rows, robust to which subjects land in the tails.
  quantile(abs(s1_cmp$pct_med), 0.9) < 18,
  # Spread: the occasion effects left in would push the P90 ~25% high.
  median(abs(s1_cmp$pct_p90)) < 12
)
```

The medians agree with Table S1 to within a few percent across all 30
rows. The rows taken exactly at 12 h, the auto-inhibition boundary, tend to
come out below the paper (by up to about 11%). Concentrations there are very sensitive to exactly when
the clearance step takes effect, because `CL/Vc` is about 2.3 1/h for
leritrelvir alone (1.25 1/h with ritonavir), so plasma follows a clearance
change within a fraction of an hour. Small differences between how NONMEM and
rxode2 time the switch around a record at 12 h are a plausible cause.

```{r figure4, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
fig4 <- sim_s1 |>
  mutate(
    Day = ifelse(time <= 24, "Day 1", "Day 5"),
    tday = ifelse(time <= 24, time, time - 96)
  ) |>
  filter(!(Day == "Day 5" & grepl("BID", Regimen) & tday > 12)) |>
  group_by(Regimen, Day, tday) |>
  summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.1), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.9), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(Panel = paste(ifelse(grepl("BID", Regimen), "BID with RTV", "TID without RTV"), "-", Day))

ggplot(fig4, aes(tday, med, colour = Regimen, fill = Regimen)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(
    data = data.frame(ec90 = c(209.7, 165), lt = c("solid", "dashed")),
    aes(yintercept = ec90, linetype = I(lt)),
    colour = "darkgreen"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Panel, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Leritrelvir (ng/mL)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Wang 2024: median and 10th-90th percentile; green lines are the EC90 targets 209.7 and 165 ng/mL.")
```

# Exposure comparison against Supplementary Table S2 (PKNCA)

Supplementary Table S2 gives geometric-mean exposures for 400 mg TID alone and
300 mg + ritonavir BID in fasted subjects, simulated by the authors from the
individual (post hoc) parameters of the 42 and 36 fasted study subjects. The
virtual cohort below (100 male and 100 female, full model including the
occasion random effects) is a different population, so exact agreement is
not expected; the geometric means nevertheless agree closely.

Units are converted to the paper's: Table S2 reports AUC per day in ng*day/mL.
For day 1 the interval is 0-24 h, so AUC(0-24) = 24 * AUC1. On day 5 the TID
interval is 96-120 h (three doses). The BID arm takes its last dose at 96 h, and
Table S2's C~min,ss~ (1047 ng/mL) is the Table S1 9th-dose trough at 108 h, so
the BID steady-state interval is the 96-108 h dosing interval and
AUC(tau) = 12 * AUCss. C~min~ is the concentration at the end of each interval,
which is how Table S2's values line up with the Table S1 troughs.

```{r tables2-sim}
s2_subj <- subjects |>
  filter(Regimen %in% c("400 mg TID", "300 mg BID + RTV"))
ev_s2 <- ev_s1 |> filter(id %in% s2_subj$id)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240912)
sim_s2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ev_s2, returnType = "data.frame", addDosing = FALSE) |>
  left_join(select(subjects, id, Regimen), by = "id")

nca_conc <- bind_rows(
  sim_s2 |> filter(time <= 24) |> mutate(Interval = "Day 1", tint = time),
  sim_s2 |>
    filter(time >= 96, time <= ifelse(grepl("BID", Regimen), 108, 120)) |>
    mutate(Interval = "Day 5", tint = time - 96)
) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, Regimen, Interval, tint, Cc)
nca_dose <- ev_s2 |>
  filter(evid == 1L, time %in% c(0, 96)) |>
  left_join(select(subjects, id, Regimen), by = "id") |>
  mutate(Interval = ifelse(time == 0, "Day 1", "Day 5"), tint = 0) |>
  select(id, Regimen, Interval, tint, amt)
nca_int <- tibble(
  Regimen = c("400 mg TID", "400 mg TID", "300 mg BID + RTV", "300 mg BID + RTV"),
  Interval = c("Day 1", "Day 5", "Day 1", "Day 5"),
  start = 0,
  end = c(24, 24, 24, 12),
  cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, clast.obs = TRUE
)
nca_s2 <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ tint | Regimen + Interval + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ tint | Regimen + Interval + id),
  intervals = as.data.frame(nca_int)
))

sim_gm <- as.data.frame(nca_s2$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast", "clast.obs")) |>
  group_by(Regimen, Interval, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(PPORRES = exp(mean(log(PPORRES))), .groups = "drop")

ref_s2 <- tribble(
  ~Regimen,           ~Interval, ~cmax, ~auclast,     ~clast.obs,
  "400 mg TID",       "Day 1",   3255,  1417 * 24,    413,
  "400 mg TID",       "Day 5",   2565,  1321 * 24,    275,
  "300 mg BID + RTV", "Day 1",   5597,  2739 * 24,   1639,
  "300 mg BID + RTV", "Day 5",   4366,  2592 * 12,   1047
)

s2_tab <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_gm,
  reference = ref_s2,
  by = c("Regimen", "Interval"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL", clast.obs = "ng/mL")
)
knitr::kable(s2_tab, digits = 0,
             caption = "Geometric means: Wang 2024 Supplementary Table S2 (fasted) vs simulation.")
attr(s2_tab, "footnote")
```

```{r tables2-gate}
s2_pct <- sim_gm |>
  inner_join(
    ref_s2 |> pivot_longer(c(cmax, auclast, clast.obs), names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("Regimen", "Interval", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * (PPORRES / ref - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(s2_pct) == 12)
stopifnot(
  abs(median(s2_pct$pct)) < 8,
  # Realised max |diff| 12.8% at the authoring seed; a cohort-level
  # transcription error in CL, F or Vc moves these by tens of percent.
  quantile(abs(s2_pct$pct), 0.9) < 22
)
```

# Food and sex effects

Supplementary Tables S2 and S3 report the fed-vs-fasted and female-vs-male
differences between different groups of study subjects, so subject-to-subject
differences are mixed into those percentages. The model's own effects are
simpler. Food multiplies F1 by exp(0.409) = 1.51, so with linear kinetics a
fed dose has 51% more AUC than the same subject fasted; the closed-form AUC
check above confirms this for the typical subject. Food also multiplies ka by
1.34 and the zero-order duration by 23.2, which moves the peak but not the
amount absorbed. The paper's simulated fed-vs-fasted differences (Table S2:
+25 to +63% alone, +29 to +34% with ritonavir) include differences between
the fed and fasted study subjects as well.

In the model, female sex lowers CL/F by a factor of exp(-0.224) = 0.80, which
raises typical exposure by 25% for both regimens. The paper's simulated
between-group differences (Table S3) are 12-17% without ritonavir and 33-51%
with ritonavir; those come from the post hoc parameters of the study subjects
and are not a clean read of the covariate effect.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Food-effect rows in Table 2 are transposed.** Table 2 lists
  `Ka.FED = 23.2` and `D1.FED = 1.34`, but the printed Results equations give
  `Ka = 0.293 * exp(0.291 * FED)` (exp(0.291) = 1.34) and
  `D1 = 0.0722 * exp(3.14 * FED)` (exp(3.14) = 23.1), and the control stream
  puts THETA(16) on D1 and THETA(17) on Ka. Table 2's rows follow THETA
  order with the labels swapped. The model follows the equations and the
  control stream: food multiplies ka by 1.34 and the zero-order duration by
  23.2.
* **Occasion variances for the 96 h occasion.** Table 2 leaves the OC2.CL and
  OC2.Vc rows blank, while the equations and the control stream include
  `OC2 * eta_OC2` on both CL and Vc. A blank row with no estimate is how a
  NONMEM `$OMEGA ... SAME` block usually appears in a results table, so the
  OC2 variances are set equal to the OC1 values (19.3% on CL, 54.4% on Vc).
  As in the control stream, OC1 stays switched on after 96 h, so from 96 h
  both the OC1 and OC2 terms apply.
* **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports IIV and occasion variability in percent. The
  95% confidence intervals are symmetric on the variance scale when the
  percentage is read as 100 * omega (CL 30.6 [23.6-36.2]:
  (23.6^2 + 36.2^2) / 2 = 933.7 = 30.6^2 to rounding; D1 155 [106-192]
  likewise), and not when it is read as a CV with omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)
  (for D1 that reading puts the midpoint at a CV of 179%). Variances are
  therefore (percent / 100)^2.
* **Random effects in the control stream but not reported.** The control
  stream carries ETA(4) on Q and ETA(7) on F1, but Table 2, the shrinkage
  footnote and the printed equations include neither. They are taken as
  fixed to zero and omitted.
* **Occasion indicators need a multiple-dose flag.** The control stream gates
  OC1 and OC2 on `DOSESCH > 1` and NONMEM `TIME` (time since the first dose).
  The model uses `MULTI_DOSE` for that flag and rxode2's `t`, so an event
  table must start at the first dose of the regimen and single-dose subjects
  must carry `MULTI_DOSE = 0`.
* **Sex coding.** The SEX coding is not printed. The paper reports higher
  exposure in females and the CL coefficient is negative, so SEX = 1 is
  female, i.e. `SEXF`.
* **Residual error.** The fed-absorption proportional error (70.2%) applies
  within 2 h of a fed dose (`tad() <= 2`), as in the control stream. The
  NONMEM floor `IPRED = 0.005` for non-positive predictions is not carried
  over.
* **Table S1 replication.** The occasion random effects are set to zero to
  match the published simulation (see above), and each arm has 200 subjects
  rather than 1000.
